title: Freeze what the two control numbers mean
points: The fleet command is (a,b): active participation and reactive injection.
Use declared voltage/current limits; inverter capability alone does not establish feeder feasibility.
caption: Native teaching diagram of the implemented fleet capability region; the point is the recorded MPC command.
note: Define S_i as each inverter’s kVA rating. The implementation requests p_i=a S_i kW and q_i=b S_i kvar using one dimensionless fleet command. Negative b means reactive absorption under the injection convention. The action validator requires 0≤a≤1, |b|≤0.44 and a²+b²≤1. These are implemented teaching bounds, not universal utility settings. Network checks separately require modeled voltage magnitudes in [0.95,1.05] p.u. and current no greater than the scenario’s rating_fraction times nominal current allowance. “100% allowed-current use” means the derated allowance is fully used, not necessarily 100% nameplate current. Freeze the backend, forecast, rating fraction, previous action and model/request revision before interpreting a result. A small negative b may help high voltage in this case, but its direction and feasibility still need a model solve. The illustrated capability region is clipped to the implemented reactive band. The marker uses rounded MPC coordinates and does not prove network feasibility. Evidence: continuous_control.py _control, map_action, ContinuousPlant.solve and verify_control; Classroom_Labs.ipynb L1 cell 4.

title: Numerical tools propose; the language model selects a trial
points: MPC solves three forecast snapshots and proposes its first move.
SAC proposes from saved trained weights. An LLM selects a permitted trial after numerical checks.
caption: Native workflow for the existing implementation; changed commands return to the solver.
note: MPC means model predictive control. Here it is a local sensitivity optimizer over H=3 quasi-static power-flow snapshots, linked by a command-movement penalty and discount 0.98. Only its first action enters the response-selection experiment. This is not a certified global optimum, dynamic stability study or robust recursive-feasibility proof. SAC means soft actor-critic: a model-free RL method. The supplied actor was trained previously using rewards from a declared OpenDSS response-surface approximation at nominal current allowance. Classroom inference uses saved weights without retraining; current derating is a transfer condition. Both tools produce candidate numerical commands. A fresh simulation and fail-closed checks decide whether a candidate can become the incumbent. Only then do actual local language models request a bounded refinement from the allowed menu. They do not solve the power flow, relax limits or grant approval. Cite the local implementation for every measured result; the MPC book and SAC paper explain the algorithm families, not performance of this feeder. Evidence: continuous_control.py optimize_mpc/sac_proposal, pilot README Roles and authority and Planning horizon versus first-action checks.
